public_sources.title: Scheduling LLM Inference with Uncertainty-Aware Output Length Predictions
public_sources.relevance: Shows stochastic/heavy-tailed output lengths, point-prediction mismatch, and tail-aware prelaunch scoring. Reports average output-length skewness 3.10, CV 1.09, P90/P50 4.62, P99/P50 10.77 across its sampled prompts, and TIE scheduling gains in its tested serving settings.

public_sources.title: Beyond Prediction: Tail-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference
public_sources.relevance: Reports that prediction-driven size scheduling can be fragile under distribution shift/bursty arrivals/memory pressure and that tail-aware prediction-free scheduling improved P99 TTLT by 35-50% versus SRPT with perfect decode-length knowledge in tested workloads.

public_sources.title: Sequential testing of conditionally constrained hypotheses
public_sources.relevance: Supports treating side information through explicit conditional null constraints; predictable affine one-step e-variables form a complete class for the conditional-hypothesis setting studied there.

synthetic_stress.status: Worker-local synthetic stress only; no deployment latency or real candidate-performance claim.
synthetic_stress.base_latency: correlated lognormal, log sigma 1.2, shared latent-task correlation component 0.45, plus independent 1% x10 side stragglers
synthetic_stress.scheduler: prelaunch fixed pair order; 32 FCFS pair slots; contiguous-prefix statistical reveal; immediate cancellation assumed for effective-occupancy metric
synthetic_stress.test: paired sign e-process with + factor 1.5, - factor 0.5, commit threshold 20, maximum 50 revealed pairs
synthetic_stress.predictor: prelaunch score X=D+noise where D is latent latency difficulty; lower score scheduled earlier; predictor does not observe paired outcome

latency_results_under_conditional_sign_i.alternative: paired sign probability q=0.75 independent of latency predictor/covariates
latency_results_under_conditional_sign_i.interpretation: When sign validity is conditional on the prelaunch ordering information, predicted-short-first can sharply reduce fixed-prefix head-of-line latency without materially changing the statistical unresolved rate in this synthetic setting.

conditional_validity_counterexample.construction: D is symmetric. Marginal null remains P(+)=0.5, but P(+|D)=logistic(-beta*D), so fast/low-D tasks favor candidate and slow/high-D tasks favor incumbent. Predictor X=D+noise is observed prelaunch and never reads the paired outcome. Sorting by X changes the prefix sign law even though the unconditional sign null remains exactly fair.
conditional_validity_counterexample.key_result: Prelaunch provenance alone is not a statistical safety condition. A predictor can be outcome-unobserving yet performance-informative. If the e-process null is only marginally valid and not valid conditional on the predictor/covariates used for ordering, predicted-short-first can massively inflate false commits.
conditional_validity_counterexample.alternative_reweighting_check: With marginal q=0.75 but q varying with D, random-order commit stayed about 0.915-0.918 while predictor-sorted prefixes reached about 0.967-0.998 across tested dependence/predictor-quality cells. Apparent power gain can therefore be task reweighting rather than only latency reduction.

measurement_validity_rules: Replace the previous rule 'prelaunch-only predictor is enough' with a stronger gate: any covariate used to choose statistical inclusion/reveal order must be covered by the conditional null, e.g. P(+|past,X)<=P(-|past,X), or the inference must explicitly condition/stratify on X.

If only marginal paired fairness is defensible, keep statistical inclusion/reveal order covariate-blind. Latency predictors may still control physical resource allocation, replication, or launch priority only insofar as those controls cannot select/reorder which signs enter the test.
Measure speed and statistical validity separately. A lower q95 wall time is not an evaluation improvement if it changes the sampled task mixture or invalidates conditional sign symmetry.

Point latency prediction is itself a fragile abstraction under heavy-tailed stochastic decoding. Compare tail-risk/distribution-aware scores and prediction-free soft-priority controls rather than treating an oracle-length sort as a deployable target.
scope_guards: All q95/occupancy/FWER values above are synthetic Monte Carlo under the stated model, not real serving measurements.
The false-commit counterexample establishes existence of a failure mode; it does not claim real evaluation latency is currently correlated with candidate advantage.

The conditional constraint required for validity depends on the actual target null and filtration; prelaunch timestamp/provenance is necessary for predictability but not sufficient for conditional exchangeability.
The oracle shortest-latency schedule was explored only as an upper-bound sanity check and is not a valid deployment assumption under stochastic LLM output lengths or resource coupling.
No conclusion here extends to outcome-dependent work stealing, race-to-first semantic replication, or resource-coupled GPU schedulers without separate validity and systems analysis.

frontier.action: Build a two-layer safe scheduler: keep a covariate-blind precommitted statistical reveal order, but use the latency predictor only for physical launch/resource/hedging decisions inside a bounded window. Quantify q95 wall and occupancy recovery relative to predictor-sorted statistical order.

In parallel derive a covariate-conditional paired-sign e-process/stratified test that permits predictor-sorted statistical order when conditional sign symmetry given predictor and frozen task covariates is explicitly modeled and falsifiable.

Replace point prediction with uncertainty-aware/tail-risk prelaunch scores, inspired by distributional output-length prediction, and stress under calibration error/distribution shift; compare to prediction-free soft priority.

Add an empirical sign-latency diagnostic protocol: frozen pre-outcome task covariates, both side completion times, pair outcome, predictor score, and candidate/incumbent identity; test whether conditional sign symmetry degrades across latency-score strata before allowing predictor-driven statistical order.

exact_next_action: Simulate the two-layer scheduler with a covariate-blind random statistical order and predictor-driven physical scheduling inside windows W in {16,32,64}; preserve the fixed reveal order exactly, compare q95 wall/effective occupancy/full-obligation occupancy against pure fixed-order launch and predictor-sorted statistical order, and verify false-commit control under the same marginal-null sign-latency counterexample.
